source.name: ASTRA Bio wave 1 — Biology in Human Welfare
source.license: Original syllabus-based practice questions (exam-frequent themes; not verbatim past papers)

questions.stem: A pathogen is best defined as an organism that
questions.explanation: Pathogens are disease-causing organisms; many are parasites that live on or in a host.

questions.stem: Amoebiasis in humans is caused by
questions.explanation: E. histolytica invades the intestinal mucosa; tetranucleate cysts in faeces spread the infection.

questions.stem: Malarial fever in man is caused by a protozoan of the genus
questions.explanation: Plasmodium species (P. vivax, P. falciparum, etc.) cause malaria after transmission by female Anopheles.

questions.stem: The common roundworm parasite of the human intestine is
questions.explanation: Ascaris is a large nematode of the small intestine; infection is by embryonated eggs in contaminated food.

questions.stem: Elephantiasis (filariasis) is produced by
questions.explanation: Adult filarial worms live in lymph vessels; blockage causes chronic swelling of limbs and scrotum.

questions.stem: Typhoid fever is caused by
questions.explanation: S. typhi is a bacterium spread by contaminated food and water; Widal test detects the infection.

questions.stem: The common cold is most often caused by
questions.explanation: Rhinoviruses infect the nose and respiratory passage; they do not usually invade the lungs.

questions.stem: Ringworm of the skin is caused by
questions.explanation: Dermatophytes (Microsporum, Trichophyton, Epidermophyton) cause ringworm; heat and moisture favour them.

questions.stem: The vector that transmits Plasmodium to humans is the
questions.explanation: Only female Anopheles takes a blood meal and injects sporozoites; Culex transmits filariasis.

questions.stem: A vaccine protects by stimulating the host to produce
questions.explanation: Antigens in a vaccine prime adaptive immunity so later infection is met by a rapid secondary response.

questions.stem: The infective stage of Entamoeba histolytica for man is the
questions.explanation: Mature quadrinucleate cysts in faecally contaminated food or water hatch into trophozoites in the intestine.

questions.stem: Haemozoin released when Plasmodium ruptures RBCs is responsible for
options: chills and high fever of malaria
questions.explanation: Haemozoin and other toxins from lysed erythrocytes trigger the cyclic fever, chill and sweating.

questions.stem: Which pairing of disease, pathogen and transmission is incorrect?
options: Amoebiasis — Entamoeba — contaminated food and water
questions.explanation: Male mosquitoes do not suck blood; malaria is transmitted by the female Anopheles.

questions.stem: Diseases that spread from an infected person to a healthy one are called
questions.explanation: Infectious diseases are caused by pathogens and can be transmitted; non-infectious ones are not contagious.

questions.stem: Houseflies can mechanically transfer Entamoeba cysts from faeces to food. Amoebiasis mainly affects the
questions.explanation: Trophozoites colonise the colon; they may cause dysentery and sometimes liver abscesses.

questions.stem: Malignant tertian malaria, the most dangerous form, is caused by
questions.explanation: P. falciparum can cause cerebral malaria; P. vivax causes benign tertian malaria.

questions.stem: Internal bleeding, muscular pain and blockage of the intestinal passage can occur in heavy infection with
questions.explanation: A mass of Ascaris in the small intestine may obstruct the gut and cause anaemia and pain.

questions.stem: Microfilariae of Wuchereria appear in peripheral blood mainly
questions.explanation: Larvae circulate in blood at night, matching the biting time of Culex, and rest in deeper vessels by day.

questions.stem: The Widal test is used in the diagnosis of
questions.explanation: Widal detects antibodies against Salmonella typhi antigens in the patient's serum.

questions.stem: HIV, the cause of AIDS, is a
questions.explanation: HIV is an RNA retrovirus that infects helper T-lymphocytes and weakens cell-mediated immunity.

questions.stem: Trichophyton, Microsporum and Epidermophyton are fungi responsible for
questions.explanation: These keratin-loving fungi infect skin, nails and scalp, producing the circular lesions of ringworm.

questions.stem: Culex mosquitoes act as vectors of
questions.explanation: Wuchereria is transmitted by Culex; Anopheles transmits Plasmodium; amoebiasis and typhoid are faecal-oral.

questions.stem: Antibodies that provide humoral immunity are produced by
questions.explanation: Activated B-cells become plasma cells that secrete immunoglobulins into blood and lymph.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about pneumonia is incorrect?
options: It may be caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae or Haemophilus influenzae
Infection is often by inhaling droplets from an infected person
Alveoli fill with fluid, impairing oxygen uptake
It is diagnosed by the Widal test
questions.explanation: Widal is for typhoid; pneumonia is a lung infection diagnosed clinically and by sputum/X-ray, not Widal.

questions.stem: Gametocytes of Plasmodium that infect the mosquito are formed in
questions.explanation: Sexual stages appear in erythrocytes; they complete gametogenesis and fertilisation in the mosquito gut.

questions.stem: Identify the incorrect statement about human parasites.
options: Ascaris eggs become infective after development in soil
Entamoeba is transmitted by female Anopheles
HIV can be transmitted by sexual contact and infected blood
questions.explanation: Entamoeba spreads by cysts in food and water, not by mosquitoes. Anopheles transmits Plasmodium.
